annotations.text:
Colour is identical in all four — the Slate preset you just shipped — so the only thing being compared here is structure.

All four stay inside what GDI can actually draw: flat fills, rounded rects, 1px rules, text and blitted thumbnails. The icons are SVG in these mockups; in the app they would be Polyline/Ellipse paths or one small blitted icon strip, since GDI has no SVG.

PALETTE — leading candidate

Axis: consolidation, keyboard-first.

One window. Pinned and Snippets become scopes instead of a second window, so there is one header, one search, one footer. The selected row grows to carry the paste modes, which stops the seven shortcuts hiding in a 12px strip. 12 rows visible vs 10 today, in a shorter window.

Tradeoff: the pinned list is no longer permanently on screen — it becomes a keystroke away.

PREVIEW

Axis: information depth.

Spends the second window on a pane that shows the whole item rather than a second list. Today you only ever see one ellipsized line — this is the direction that fixes that. Pinned moves inline as a section header.

Tradeoff: wants 900px of width, and the pane is dead weight when all you want is the item you just copied.

DENSE

Axis: density.

18 rows in the same 560px where the current design fits 10. Real columns, hairline rules, and the outlined letter badge collapses to a 3-character type code. This is the direction closest to the app's AS/400 heritage.

Tradeoff: no room for a preview or inline actions, and image thumbnails would have to shrink or go.

QUICK PICK

Axis: footprint.

Opens at the text caret for the case that is most of the use — take one of the last six copies and carry on typing. Press the digit, it pastes.

Tradeoff: no browsing, no search, no pinning. This is a companion to one of the other three, not a replacement for it.
